description: SEND `exitAmountUsd` WITH THE POSITION YOU ARE WEIGHING and this answers whether that size has ever cleared here: the schema has carried it since 2026-10-08, and an auditor still had to find it by guessing because this sentence did not say so. Without it the answer still describes the capacity; with it, `exitCapacity` says `covered-now`, `above-declared` or `unknown` for your amount, and whether a single withdrawal that large has ever been recorded. Before putting capital somewhere, ask what has actually LEFT it. Every liquidity figure elsewhere is a level at an instant — how much could be withdrawn right now. This is the other half: withdrawals that SETTLED, over 7, 30 and 90 days, with the largest single exit we have ever recorded and the day it happened. Measured on the largest vault we read: $52.8M declared withdrawable against $265.8M actually withdrawn over thirty days, so a holder reading only the declared figure would badly underestimate what the vault has been able to pay. A LEVEL and a FLOW are never divided by one another and this returns no ratio between them. We see withdrawals that settled and NOT an attempt that reverted, a queue somebody waited in, or a gate that refused them. An empty register therefore has FOUR readings, not two: “nobody withdrew”, “nobody could”, “a reader asked and found nothing at all”, and “no reader has ever asked”. `haveFlowHistory` separates the first two from the last two and `lastReadAt` separates those — null there means nobody has ever looked, so the register is not a weak reading of the vault but the absence of one. `haveFlowHistory` separates the third from the first two, and where it is false every figure is NULL rather than zero. Every answer dates itself: `capitalAsOf` and `declaredAsOf` say when each level was read, `flowsNewestAt` how far our movement history reaches, and `windowsEndAt` the instant the windows count back from. For a capital decision the age of the record is part of the record. Free.

exitAmountUsd.description: OPTIONAL, AND THE ANSWER IS USEFUL WITHOUT IT: send nothing and `exitCapacity` still describes the capacity — what the vault declares withdrawable right now, the largest single withdrawal ever recorded here, the basis and when it was read — with `amountUsd`, `now`, `everThisLarge` and `shareOfDeclared` null, because those are the three answers that need a position and NOBODY ASKED is not the same as nothing here. Send a position, in US dollars, e.g. 500000, and you get the verdict for THAT amount. Turns "can we READ the withdrawable figure" into "could I get THIS much back out". The verdict is deliberately named for what was observed rather than for a promise: `covered-now` means the amount is inside what the vault declares withdrawable AT THE MOMENT WE READ IT, and the answer carries when that was and what it cannot see — queues, notice periods, failed attempts, other holders leaving at the same time.

slug.description: The vault’s slug, or its contract address — either resolves. Until 2026-10-08 this route was the one of eight that took the slug only, so an agent holding an address got a 404 here and a 200 everywhere else.

name: vault_exits

cannotSee.description: What this register structurally cannot contain, so an empty one is never read as an easy exit.

capitalAsOf.description: When `tvlUsd` was read. Same name and same column as `vault_check` uses.

declaredAsOf.description: When `declaredWithdrawableUsd` was read. NULL means we hold no stamp for it rather than that it is fresh — 180 of the 809 declared levels we hold come from a writer that does not stamp them.

declaredWithdrawableUsd.description: A LEVEL at this instant. Null where we cannot read it, which is not zero.

exitCap.description: THE CONTRACT ASKED DIRECTLY, ON THE VAULTS THAT DECLARE NOTHING. Present only where `declaredWithdrawableUsd` is null, which is where 33 Concrete vaults holding $1.26bn and the ether.fi Liquid vaults sit: a strategy vault deploys its capital rather than holding it, so there is no free balance to read and the venue publishes no withdrawable figure. We call `maxWithdraw` on the LARGEST HOLDER WE KNOW — per owner, so asked about an address holding no shares it answers zero for every vault in existence, which is why it must never be asked of a stranger — and compare it with what that holder’s shares are worth. READ `verdict` BEFORE ANY NUMBER HERE. `capped` means the contract returned LESS than the holding, so something binds and `maxWithdrawUnits` is where it binds. `shut` means it returned zero to a holder who demonstrably has shares, which is a finding and not an absence. `echoes-balance` means it returned the holding itself: the selector carries NO liquidity cap, so the figure is arithmetic about that holder and not a reading of the vault, and we publish it as a refusal — `maxWithdrawUsd` is null and reading the units as withdrawable capacity would be wrong. `unanswered` is our silence, not the vault’s. `saysSomethingAboutExit` is the single boolean to gate on. It is ONE HOLDER at ONE BLOCK, never a vault-wide total and never a promise; `raw` carries the three words so the verdict can be re-derived rather than believed.

exitCapacity.description: ALWAYS PRESENT for a vault we hold. `basis` names what it rests on: `observed-liquidity` means a figure the VENUE declared and we read at `declaredAsOf`, and nothing else — it is not a promise, not a test of whether the vault would pay, and not a reading of any queue. WITHOUT `exitAmountUsd` it is the capacity alone: `declaredWithdrawableUsd` and `largestEverUsd`, with `amountUsd`, `now`, `everThisLarge` and `shareOfDeclared` all null because no position was named. WITH one, those four answer the fit. TWO READINGS, NEVER AVERAGED: `now` is `covered-now`, `above-declared` or `unknown` against what the vault declares withdrawable at this instant — THEIR figure, an instant and not a promise, and not a queue or a notice period; `everThisLarge` is whether a single withdrawal at least that size has ever been recorded here, and it is NULL rather than false where we hold no flow history, because never having seen one is not evidence it cannot happen. `shareOfDeclared` is the position as a share of that declared figure, null where there is nothing to divide by. `cannotSee` names what no withdrawable figure contains: queues, notice periods, failed attempts, and other holders leaving at the same moment as you.

exitPhases.description: GETTING OUT HAS THREE STEPS AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME EVENT: a request FILED, an amount set aside to be CLAIMED, and a withdrawal SETTLED. Each carries its own `basis` and its own refusal. `filed` reads `queue-requests` where the vault leaves through a separate queue - a FLOOR, since a request whose only event predates our window is open and unseen - or `share-burns` where it is read from the token being burned. `claimable` IS USUALLY UNREADABLE AND THAT IS THE FINDING: where a vault takes a request and carries neither ERC-7540 getter, nothing can be seen of the middle step at all and a zero there would be an answer we did not read; where both getters exist it is readable one holder at a time and NO TOTAL is published, because summing a per-holder getter across holders we do not enumerate is a figure nobody could check; a synchronous vault has no middle step to begin with. `settled` is money that LEFT, over the register’s own window, not money that was promised.

flowsNewestAnywhereAt.description: The newest movement we hold for ANY vault. Read beside the field above it tells a quiet vault from a stopped reader, which is what every zero here turns on.

flowsNewestAt.description: The newest movement of any kind we hold for this vault.

haveFlowHistory.description: Whether we hold ANY movement for this vault, of either direction. FALSE means the empty register is our silence and not the vault’s: it says nothing about whether anybody got out. Of 3,672 open vaults on 2026-10-10, 2,673 are in this state.

largestEverAt.description: When `largestEverUsd` was taken out. An old date beside a large figure is the whole point: it says the exit was possible then, not now.

largestEverUsd.description: Somebody actually got this much out, on `largestEverAt`. Evidence about the past, never a promise about now.

lastReadAt.description: When a reader last ASKED about this vault, found or not — which `flowsNewestAt` cannot tell you. Eighteen withdrawals with the newest eleven months ago is a vault that went quiet OR a vault we stopped reading, and only this separates them. NULL MEANS NO READER HAS EVER ASKED: the vault is outside what our flow readers cover, so an empty register is not a weak reading of it, it is the absence of one.

meta.description: How current this answer is and what it was read from: `freshness` and the ages behind it. Present on every answer from this server, whatever the tool.

readToBlock.description: How far through the chain that pass actually got. Not the same as `lastReadAt`: a reader that ran a minute ago but is 400,000 blocks behind looked recently at an old part of the chain, and only this says so. Null where the reader has no block to report.

redemption.description: HOW a holder gets out, read from the contract, and the question no liquidity figure answers. `mechanic` is `synchronous`, `request-and-claim` (ERC-7540: you ask and are paid when the vault settles it), `request-via-queue` (the vault takes deposits and carries no exit: you approve a SEPARATE queue contract and file a request there for somebody else to fill) or `unread`. `paused` is the contract’s own switch. `hours` is a notice period the contract STATES, null where it states none, which is NOT zero. Same object and same wording as `vault_check` returns.

redemptionIntelligence.description: GETTING OUT, AS ONE ORDERED THING. The same readings as the sibling blocks, composed in the order a depositor meets them and computing nothing of its own, so it cannot disagree with them: mechanism (how leaving works here at all), capacity (whether there is anything to leave with), filed (whether a request has to be made and who is ahead of you), claimable (whether what is owed has been set aside), settled (whether anybody has actually been paid). START HERE and read the parts for detail. Each step carries `applies`, `readable`, `basis`, `reading`, `usd` and `says`, and the two flags are NOT the same thing: `applies: false` means the step does not exist on this vault at all — a synchronous redemption settles in the transaction that asks for it, so there is no request and nothing is ever set aside — while `readable: false` on a step that applies is a gap in OUR reading or the contract’s silence. `weakestLink` names the first step that exists here and that we cannot see, and is the single most useful field on this answer: a chain is only as good as its first unreadable step, and every step after it is conditional on something we could not establish. `readableSteps` of `applicableSteps` says how much of the sequence we have.

says.description: What actually left, against what the vault advertises as withdrawable, in one sentence.

sharesLeft.description: WHO LEFT, WHERE OUR FLOW REGISTER CANNOT SEE IT, read from the chain. A `Flow` row is written when a reader recognises a venue’s withdrawal, and some venues pay out by BURNING the holder’s shares and emitting nothing we recognise — one $14M vault had 885.30 shares leave in sixty days while the register held six deposits and not one exit. A share burned is a holder leaving, because nothing else destroys supply. `burns` and `shares` are the exits that settled, `shareOfSupply` scales them against what the vault holds in shares TODAY (so it is a scale, not a rate: the two are of different moments). `filed` is requests to leave read in the same window, NULL where the vault has no queue to file one in rather than zero. `oldestWaitingDays` is how long the front of the queue has waited with no payout behind it and `medianSettlementDays` how long a wait that ended actually took — both under ONE assumption which `assumes` states: requests settle in the order filed and one payout settles one. Both are FLOORS, because a request filed before the window is older than this can see. NO DOLLAR FIGURE on purpose: pricing a burn needs the share price at that block and the asset’s price at that moment, and a number built from two interpolations would be the most confident thing in the answer. Published BESIDE the register and never summed into it.

slug.description: The vault this register is for, read back so an answer cannot be attached to the wrong vault.

tvlUsd.description: What the vault holds, for scale beside the withdrawals. A LEVEL, never to be divided into the flow figures in `windows`. Null means unread, not empty.

venueWithdrawable.description: WHAT THE VENUE’S OWN ACCOUNTING SAYS ABOUT FREE LIQUIDITY, AGAINST OURS. Null where no venue API has been read for this vault. `theirShare` and `ourShare` are both shares of the vault, never dollars — ours is derived in dollars and theirs is in asset units, and converting one would put a third party’s price into a comparison of two first-party readings. `agreement` is `agrees` (within a tenth of each other), `ours-is-higher`, `ours-is-lower` or `not-compared`, and a missing reading is NEVER an agreement. Measured on the first pass over Morpho V2: 112 vaults agree, and on 87 holding $1.73bn ours is on average 40.7 percentage points HIGHER than the vault’s own figure — read the lower one before planning an exit. `timelockSeconds` is a notice period the VENUE states, which is a different kind of evidence from the one our own contract walk measures and is reported as theirs.

warnings.description: Anything the server wants a caller to know about THIS answer before acting on it. Empty is the normal case and is not a guarantee.

windows.description: FLOWS over 7, 30 and 90 days plus all time: count, total, largest single, most recent. Never a share of the level. Every figure is NULL where `haveFlowHistory` is false, because a zero would claim we looked. Each window carries `window` as well as `days`: `7d`, `30d`, `90d` or `allTime`. `days: 0` is the all-time one and reads as a zero-day window if you only look at the number, which is why the name is there.

windowsEndAt.description: The instant every window counts back from, so the 7-day and 30-day figures share an edge and either can be reproduced. It is a window boundary and NOT a freshness claim: the ages of the data are `capitalAsOf`, `declaredAsOf` and `flowsNewestAt`, and `meta.freshness` is computed from those.

title: What actually left a vault
